body.statement:
For every \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) and every integer \(k\geq2\),
\[
 m_k-\beta c_k=\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k\in A,
 \qquad Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k.
\]
These identities require only finite moments through order \(k\), source independence, and the maintained latent-profile plane; no global moment generating function is used.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\), an environment \(e\), and an integer \(k\geq2\).  The all-orders moment condition in the definition of \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) implies that every product moment occurring below is finite.  For random variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\), the joint cumulant is the finite moment--cumulant polynomial
\[
 \operatorname{cum}(X_1,\ldots,X_k)
 =\sum_{\pi\in\mathfrak P_k}
 (|\pi|-1)!(-1)^{|\pi|-1}
 \prod_{D\in\pi}\mathbb E\!\left[\prod_{j\in D}X_j\right],
 \tag{1}
\]
where \(\mathfrak P_k\) is the set of partitions of \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\).  Each variable occurs exactly once in each monomial in (1), so (1) is linear in each argument.  If the arguments can be split into two nonempty independent groups, substitution of the corresponding factorization of every block moment into (1) gives zero.  Equivalently, in the truncated formal moment series the coefficient in (1) is the coefficient of the corresponding monomial in the formal logarithm; independence factors the moment series, and
\(\log(M_1M_2)=\log M_1+\log M_2\) has no monomial involving variables from both groups.  This argument is purely polynomial through total degree \(k\) and does not require an analytic moment generating function.

The structural equations give
\[
 T_e=\alpha U_e+\epsilon_{t,e},
 \qquad
 Y_e=\beta T_e+\gamma U_e+\epsilon_y.
 \tag{2}
\]
Apply separate linearity of (1) to the mixed cumulant with one \(Y_e\) argument and \(k-1\) copies of \(T_e\).  Because \(\epsilon_y\) is independent of \((U_e,\epsilon_{t,e})\), and hence of \(T_e\), the independent-groups consequence of (1) makes its term vanish.  Therefore
\[
 \kappa_k(Y_e,T_e,\ldots,T_e)
 =\beta\kappa_k(T_e)+
   \gamma\kappa_k(U_e,T_e,\ldots,T_e).
 \tag{3}
\]
Expanding the last \(k-1\) arguments by the first equation in (2), every term containing both \(U_e\) and \(\epsilon_{t,e}\) vanishes by their independence.  The only surviving term is the all-\(U_e\) term, and thus
\[
 \kappa_k(U_e,T_e,\ldots,T_e)
 =\alpha^{k-1}\kappa_k(U_e)
 =\alpha^{k-1}\kappa_k(\epsilon_{u,e}).
 \tag{4}
\]
Combining (3)--(4) and subtracting the corresponding equality for the reference environment \(0\), the definitions of \(m_k,c_k,u_k\) yield, coordinate by coordinate,
\[
 m_k=\beta c_k+\alpha^{k-1}\gamma u_k.
 \tag{5}
\]
The latent-profile condition in \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\) gives \(u_k\in A\), and scalar multiplication preserves membership in a linear subspace.  Hence the second term on the right of (5) belongs to \(A\).  Since \(Q_A\) is the orthogonal-complement projector, \(Q_Au_k=0\).  Applying \(Q_A\) to (5) proves
\[
 Q_Am_k=\beta Q_Ac_k,
\]
as asserted.
